questionText: An ideal gas expands from volume 2 L to 6 L at a constant pressure of 3 × 10⁵ N/m². The work done by the gas is:

subject: Physics
questionText: A refrigerator has a coefficient of performance of 5. If it absorbs 250 J of heat from the cold compartment per cycle, the work done on the refrigerator per cycle is:

subject: Physics
questionText: During an adiabatic compression, the volume of a diatomic gas (γ = 1.4) is reduced to 1/32 of its initial volume. If the initial temperature is 300 K, the final temperature is:

subject: Physics
questionText: In a thermodynamic process, 200 J of heat is added to a system and 80 J of work is done by the system. The change in internal energy of the system is:
explanation: First law of thermodynamics: ΔQ = ΔU + W => ΔU = ΔQ - W = 200 J - 80 J = 120 J.

subject: Physics
questionText: A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at 127°C and a cold reservoir at 27°C. If it absorbs 800 J of heat per cycle from the hot reservoir, the work done per cycle is:

subject: Physics
questionText: When 100 g of ice at 0°C is mixed with 100 g of water at 80°C in a thermally insulated vessel (L_ice = 80 cal/g, c_water = 1 cal/g°C), the final temperature of the mixture is:
explanation: Heat needed to melt 100 g ice at 0°C = 100 × 80 = 8000 cal. Heat available from 100 g water cooling from 80°C to 0°C = 100 × 1 × 80 = 8000 cal. Thus all ice just melts and final temperature is 0°C.

subject: Physics
questionText: A blackbody at 27°C radiates thermal energy at a rate of E W/m². At what temperature (in °C) will it radiate energy at a rate of 16 E W/m²?
explanation: E ∝ T⁴. Here T₁ = 27 + 273 = 300 K. Since E₂/E₁ = (T₂/T₁)⁴ = 16 = 2⁴ => T₂ = 2 T₁ = 600 K = 327°C.

subject: Physics
questionText: A body cools from 80°C to 64°C in 5 minutes and to 52°C in the next 5 minutes (total 10 minutes). Using Newton's law of cooling (average form), the temperature of the surroundings is:

subject: Physics
questionText: An ideal monoatomic gas (γ = 5/3) is compressed adiabatically to 1/8th of its initial volume. If its initial temperature is 27°C (300 K), its final temperature will be:
explanation: For an adiabatic process, T₁ V₁^(γ-1) = T₂ V₂^(γ-1). With γ - 1 = 2/3 and V₁/V₂ = 8: T₂ = 300 × (8)^(2/3) = 300 × 4 = 1200 K.

subject: Physics
questionText: During an adiabatic expansion of 2 moles of an ideal gas, the internal energy of the gas is found to decrease by 100 J. The work done during the process by the gas is:
explanation: In an adiabatic process, Q = 0. By First Law Q = ΔU + W => 0 = (-100 J) + W => W = +100 J.

subject: Physics
questionText: A Carnot refrigerator has a coefficient of performance β = 5. If the temperature inside the freezer is -13°C (260 K), the temperature of the surrounding room to which heat is rejected is:

subject: Physics
questionText: The wavelength of maximum emission (λ_m) for the Sun is approximately 475 nm (given Wien's constant b = 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K). The effective surface temperature of the Sun is approximately:

subject: Physics
questionText: A metal rod of length 2 m expands by 2 mm when heated from 20°C to 120°C. Calculate coefficient of linear expansion α.

subject: Physics
questionText: First law of thermodynamics is a statement of:
explanation: ΔU = Q − W: heat absorbed equals change in internal energy plus work done.

subject: Physics
questionText: In an isothermal process, temperature remains constant so:
explanation: For ideal gas, U depends on T only; isothermal → ΔT = 0 → ΔU = 0.

subject: Physics
questionText: Efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between T₁ and T₂ (T₁ > T₂) is:
explanation: η = 1 − T₂/T₁ (T in Kelvin).

subject: Physics
questionText: Which process has no heat exchange with surroundings?
explanation: Adiabatic process: Q = 0, so all energy change is via work only.

subject: Physics
questionText: Second law of thermodynamics implies:
options: Heat cannot flow spontaneously from cold to hot
explanation: Entropy of universe increases; heat flows spontaneously only from hot to cold.

subject: Physics
questionText: Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics establishes the concept of:
options: Temperature (if systems A and B are in thermal equilibrium with C, then A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other)
explanation: Zeroth law provides the theoretical basis for temperature measurement via thermometry.

subject: Physics
questionText: In an Isothermal process for an ideal gas, temperature remains constant (ΔT = 0). The change in internal energy (ΔU) is:
options: Zero (ΔU = n Cv ΔT = 0, so Q = W)
explanation: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature; at constant T, ΔU = 0, hence heat added equals work done (Q = W).

subject: Physics
questionText: For an Adiabatic process of an ideal gas, the equation of state is:
options: P V^γ = Constant, T V^(γ-1) = Constant, and T^γ P^(1-γ) = Constant (where γ = Cp / Cv)
explanation: Adiabatic governing equation: P V^γ = constant, where γ is the adiabatic index (Cp/Cv).

subject: Physics
questionText: Work done in an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas from (P1, V1, T1) to (P2, V2, T2) is:

subject: Physics
questionText: The slope of an Adiabatic curve on a P-V indicator diagram is steeper than that of an Isothermal curve by a factor of:
explanation: Isothermal slope = -P/V; Adiabatic slope = -γ(P/V) = γ × Isothermal slope.

subject: Physics
questionText: Carnot Engine is an ideal reversible heat engine operating between hot reservoir (T1) and cold reservoir (T2). Its thermal efficiency (η) is:
explanation: Sadi Carnot (1824): Efficiency of reversible heat engine depends only on temperatures of source and sink in Kelvin: η = 1 - T_sink/T_source.

subject: Physics
questionText: Coefficient of Performance (β or COP) of an ideal Carnot refrigerator operating between T1 (hot) and T2 (cold) is:
explanation: COP β = Heat extracted from cold sink / Work input = T2 / (T1 - T2).

subject: Physics
questionText: Kelvin-Planck statement of Second Law of Thermodynamics rules out:
options: A 100% efficient heat engine that converts absorbed heat completely into work without rejecting heat to a cold reservoir
explanation: It is impossible to construct an engine whose sole effect is extracting heat from a single reservoir and doing equivalent work (Perpetual Motion Machine of 2nd kind).

subject: Physics
questionText: Clausius statement of Second Law of Thermodynamics rules out:
options: Heat transfer from hot to cold
Spontaneous transfer of heat from a colder body to a hotter body without external work input
explanation: Heat cannot flow spontaneously from lower to higher temperature without consuming external mechanical work.

subject: Physics
questionText: The area enclosed by a cyclic process on a P-V indicator diagram represents:
options: Net work done during one complete thermodynamic cycle (W_net = ∮ P dV)
explanation: Net work done per cycle equals the enclosed area of the P-V closed loop (positive if clockwise, negative if counter-clockwise).

subject: Physics
questionText: In an Isochoric (constant volume) thermodynamic process, work done (W) and heat exchanged (Q) are:
options: W = 0 and Q = ΔU = n Cv ΔT
explanation: Since ΔV = 0, work done W = ∫ P dV = 0, so all heat supplied changes internal energy: Q = ΔU = n Cv ΔT.

subject: Physics
questionText: For an ideal monoatomic gas (γ = 5/3) expanding at constant pressure (Isobaric process), the fraction of heat supplied that is converted into work (W/Q) is:
explanation: For monoatomic gas: W/Q = (γ - 1)/γ = (5/3 - 1)/(5/3) = (2/3)/(5/3) = 2/5 (40%). The remaining 60% increases internal energy (ΔU/Q = 3/5).

subject: Physics
questionText: For a general polytropic process P V^x = Constant, the molar heat capacity C of an ideal gas is:
explanation: For PVⁿ = constant: C = Cv + R/(1 - n).

subject: Physics
questionText: During free expansion of an ideal gas into an insulated vacuum container:
options: Temperature remains constant (ΔT = 0, ΔU = 0, W = 0, Q = 0), but Entropy increases (ΔS > 0)
explanation: Free expansion is irreversible: no heat enters, no work is done (W=0, Q=0, ΔU=0 => ΔT=0 for ideal gas), and entropy increases (ΔS = nR ln(V2/V1) > 0).

subject: Physics
questionText: A quasi-static thermodynamic process is an idealized process that is carried out:
options: Infinitely slowly such that the system remains in thermodynamic equilibrium with its surroundings at all times
explanation: Quasi-static ('near-static') processes proceed through a continuous sequence of equilibrium states.

subject: Physics
questionText: According to the Third Law of Thermodynamics, the heat capacity (Cp and Cv) of all solids approaches what value as T -> 0 K?
options: 0 (Zero, Debye T^3 law for non-magnetic insulators)
explanation: At T -> 0 K, thermal vibrational modes freeze out quantum mechanically, so heat capacity C -> 0.

subject: Physics
questionText: If the door of an operational domestic refrigerator is kept open in a closed room with all windows shut, the temperature of the room will:
options: Increase (Net heat rejected to room Q1 = Q2 + W exceeds heat extracted Q2 by electrical work W)
explanation: Refrigerator motor expends work W and exhausts (Q2 + W) into the room, causing net room heating.

subject: Physics
questionText: The Triple Point of Water (where ice, liquid water, and water vapor coexist in stable thermodynamic equilibrium) is standardly defined as:
options: 273.16 K (0.01°C) at a partial vapor pressure of 611.65 Pa (4.58 mm Hg)
explanation: The triple point of water is unique and fixed at exactly 273.16 K (0.01°C) and 4.58 mm Hg (611.65 Pa).

subject: Physics
questionText: Latent heat of fusion of ice (Lf) and latent heat of vaporization of water (Lv) are approximately:
explanation: Vaporization requires breaking all intermolecular hydrogen bonds, so Lv (540 cal/g) is ~6.75 times larger than Lf (80 cal/g).

subject: Physics
questionText: When water is heated from 0°C to 10°C, its volume:
options: Decreases from 0°C to 4°C, reaches a minimum at 4°C (maximum density), and then increases from 4°C to 10°C
explanation: Anomalous expansion of water: volume is minimum and density is maximum (1.000 g/cm³) at 4°C.

subject: Physics
questionText: A refrigerator is a heat engine working in?
explanation: Refrigerator is a reverse heat engine (absorbs work to move heat).

subject: Physics
questionText: Newton's First Law of Motion defines which physical property?
explanation: First law (Law of Inertia) defines inertia: inability of a body to change its state of rest or motion by itself.

subject: Physics
questionText: Newton's Second Law gives quantitative measure of:
explanation: Second law states rate of change of momentum is proportional to applied force, providing F = ma.

subject: Physics
questionText: In an ISOTHERMAL process, which parameter of ideal gas remains constant?
explanation: Isothermal process occurs at constant temperature, so internal energy change ΔU = 0.

subject: Physics
questionText: Carnot engine working between temperatures T1 (source) and T2 (sink) has efficiency η equal to:
explanation: Carnot efficiency η = (T1 - T2) / T1 = 1 - (T2 / T1).

subject: Physics
questionText: For an ADIABATIC process, the relation between P and V is:
explanation: Adiabatic gas equation is P V^γ = constant, where γ = CP / CV.

subject: Physics
questionText: Kirchhoff's First Law (Junction rule Σ I = 0) is a conservation law of:
explanation: Junction rule states total current entering a node equals current leaving, expressing conservation of charge.

subject: Physics
questionText: Kirchhoff's Second Law (Loop rule Σ V = 0) is a conservation law of:
explanation: Loop rule states algebraic sum of potential changes around closed loop is zero (conservation of energy).

subject: Physics
questionText: Temperature of sink of a Carnot engine with 50% efficiency is 7°C. To increase efficiency to 70%, by how much should source temperature be increased?

subject: Physics
questionText: An ideal gas undergoes adiabatic expansion such that P ∝ T³. Find the ratio of specific heats γ.
explanation: For adiabatic rxn P¹⁻γ Tγ = const => P ∝ Tγ/⁽γ⁻¹⁾. γ/(γ-1) = 3 => γ = 3γ - 3 => 2γ = 3 => γ = 1.5.

subject: Physics
questionText: When an ideal diatomic gas (γ = 7/5) expands at constant pressure (isobaric process), the fraction of the heat energy supplied that is used in doing external work (W / Q) is:
explanation: In an isobaric process, W / Q = (n R ΔT) / (n C_P ΔT) = R / C_P = (γ - 1) / γ = (7/5 - 1) / (7/5) = 2 / 7.

subject: Physics
questionText: Two rods of identical length and cross-sectional area, having thermal conductivities K₁ and K₂, are connected in parallel between two heat reservoirs. The effective thermal conductivity of the combination is:
explanation: In parallel, H = H₁ + H₂ => K_eq (2A) ΔT / L = (K₁ A + K₂ A) ΔT / L => K_eq = (K₁ + K₂) / 2.

subject: Physics
questionText: The triple point of water is the unique temperature and pressure at which solid ice, liquid water, and water vapour coexist in thermal equilibrium. Its values are:
explanation: The standard triple point of water is T_tr = 273.16 K (0.01°C) and P_tr = 611.65 Pa (0.006 atm = 4.58 mm Hg).

subject: Physics
questionText: In a free expansion of an ideal gas into an evacuated chamber (adiabatic container with rigid walls):
options: Q = 0, W = 0, and ΔU = 0 (temperature remains unchanged)
explanation: Against vacuum P_ext = 0 so W = 0; walls are adiabatic so Q = 0; hence ΔU = 0 and ΔT = 0 for an ideal gas.

subject: Physics
questionText: A brass disc has a circular hole in its center. If the disc is heated uniformly, the diameter of the central hole will:
explanation: Thermal expansion is like a photographic enlargement: every linear dimension, including cavity/hole diameters, increases by (1 + α ΔT).

subject: Physics
questionText: The specific heat capacity of a gas during an isothermal process is:
explanation: Since C = Q / (n ΔT) and ΔT = 0 while Q ≠ 0 in an isothermal process, C_isothermal = ∞ (whereas C_adiabatic = 0).

subject: Physics
questionText: A thermodynamic system is taken through a clockwise circular cycle on a P-V diagram where pressure P varies between 100 kPa and 300 kPa and volume V varies between 1 L and 3 L. The net work done per cycle is:
explanation: Area of ellipse/circle = π (ΔP/2)(ΔV/2) = π (100 × 10³ Pa)(1 × 10⁻³ m³) = 100 π J.

subject: Physics
questionText: Which of the following processes is a thermodynamic IRREVERSIBLE process?
options: Quasi-static isothermal expansion of an ideal gas
Quasi-static adiabatic compression of a frictionless piston
Joule heating of a resistor by electric current and free expansion of a gas
explanation: Dissipative effects like Joule heating, friction, viscosity, and unrestrained free expansion are irreversible.

subject: Physics
questionText: If the coefficient of linear expansion of a pendulum rod is α, the fractional loss of time (Δt / t) per second when the ambient temperature rises by ΔT is:
explanation: Since T = 2π√(L/g) ∝ L^(1/2), ΔT_period / T_period = ½ (ΔL / L) = ½ α ΔT.

subject: Physics
questionText: A body cools from 80°C to 60°C in 5 minutes when surrounding temperature is 20°C. Assuming Newton's law of cooling (average form), how long will it take to cool from 60°C to 40°C in the same surroundings?
explanation: By Newton's law of cooling: (T1 - T2)/t = K × ((T1 + T2)/2 - T0). For the first interval: (80 - 60)/5 = K × (70 - 20) => 4 = 50 K => K = 0.08 min^-1. For the second interval: (60 - 40)/t2 = K × (50 - 20) => 20 / t2 = 0.08 × 30 = 2.4 => t2 = 20 / 2.4 = 8.33 minutes.

subject: Physics
questionText: Two soap bubbles of radii r1 and r2 coalesce under isothermal conditions in vacuum into a single spherical soap bubble of radius R. The radius R is given by:
explanation: In vacuum (external pressure P0 = 0), conservation of moles under isothermal conditions gives n1 + n2 = n => P1 V1 + P2 V2 = P V. Since excess pressure inside a soap bubble is P = 4T/r and volume V = (4/3) × pi × r^3, the product P × V is proportional to r^2. Therefore, r1^2 + r2^2 = R^2 => R = sqrt(r1^2 + r2^2).

subject: Physics
questionText: A Carnot heat engine operates between a source at 600 K and a sink at 300 K. Its output work is used to drive a Carnot refrigerator operating between 250 K (cold reservoir) and 300 K (room temperature). If the heat engine absorbs 1000 J of heat per cycle from the 600 K source, how much heat is extracted per cycle from the 250 K cold reservoir by the refrigerator?
explanation: 1) Efficiency of Carnot engine: eta = 1 - T_sink / T_source = 1 - 300/600 = 0.50. Work output of engine W = eta × Q1 = 0.50 × 1000 J = 500 J. 2) Coefficient of Performance (COP) of Carnot refrigerator between T_c = 250 K and T_h = 300 K: beta = T_c / (T_h - T_c) = 250 / (300 - 250) = 250 / 50 = 5.0. 3) Heat extracted from cold reservoir Q_c = beta × W = 5.0 × 500 J = 2500 J.

subject: Physics
questionText: Heat given to a system is 100 J and work done by the system is 40 J. The change in internal energy is?
explanation: delta U = Q - W = 100 - 40 = 60 J.

subject: Physics
questionText: Wien's Displacement Law states that wavelength of maximum emission (λm) is related to absolute temperature T as:
explanation: Wien's Law: λm ∝ 1/T => λm T = b (Wien's constant b = 2.898 x 10^-3 m K).

subject: Physics
questionText: Which has the maximum efficiency theoretically?
explanation: Carnot engine is an ideal engine with maximum possible efficiency.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the molecular speeds in Column I with their formulas in Column II (M: molar mass, T: temperature, k: Boltzmann constant):
Column I:
(A) Root Mean Square Speed (v_rms)
(B) Average Speed (v_avg)
(C) Most Probable Speed (v_mp)
(D) Ratio v_mp : v_avg : v_rms
Column II:
(1) √(3 R T / M)
(2) √(8 R T / π M)
(3) √(2 R T / M)
(4) 1 : 1.128 : 1.224 (√2 : √(8/π) : √3)
explanation: v_rms = √(3RT/M); v_avg = √(8RT/πM); v_mp = √(2RT/M). Ranking: v_mp < v_avg < v_rms.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the gas types in Column I with their degrees of freedom (f) at room temperature in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Monoatomic gas (He, Ne, Ar)
(B) Diatomic gas (rigid rotator, O₂, N₂)
(C) Non-linear triatomic gas (H₂O, SO₂)
(D) Diatomic gas with vibrational mode at high T
Column II:
(1) 3 (translational only)
(2) 5 (3 trans + 2 rot)
(3) 6 (3 trans + 3 rot)
(4) 7 (3 trans + 2 rot + 2 vib)
explanation: Degrees of freedom: monoatomic = 3; rigid diatomic = 5; non-linear triatomic = 6; high-T vibrating diatomic = 7.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the kinetic theory parameters in Column I with their mathematical formulas in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Pressure of an ideal gas
(B) Average kinetic energy of one molecule
(C) Mean free path (λ)
(D) Boltzmann constant (k_B)
Column II:
(1) ⅓ ρ v_rms²
(2) 3/2 k_B T
(3) 1 / (√2 π n d²)
(4) R / N_A
explanation: P = 1/3 ρ v_rms²; kinetic energy per molecule = 3/2 k_B T; mean free path λ = 1/(√2 π n d²).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the gas laws in Column I with their constant variables in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Boyle's Law
(B) Charles's Law
(C) Gay-Lussac's Law
(D) Avogadro's Law
Column II:
(1) Temperature constant (P ∝ 1/V)
(2) Pressure constant (V ∝ T)
(3) Volume constant (P ∝ T)
(4) P and T constant (V ∝ n)
explanation: Boyle: T const; Charles: P const; Gay-Lussac: V const; Avogadro: equal volumes of all gases at same P and T have equal molecules.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the specific heat capacities in Column I with their expressions in terms of gas constant R in Column II:
Column I:
(A) C_v for monoatomic gas
(B) C_p for monoatomic gas
(C) C_v for rigid diatomic gas
(D) C_p for rigid diatomic gas
Column II:
(1) 3/2 R
(2) 5/2 R
(3) 5/2 R
(4) 7/2 R
explanation: C_v = f/2 R; C_p = C_v + R = (f/2 + 1) R. Monoatomic (f=3) gives 3/2R and 5/2R; diatomic (f=5) gives 5/2R and 7/2R.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following ideal gas types with their degrees of freedom (f) and adiabatic index (γ = 1 + 2/f) at room temperature:
Column I:
(A) Monoatomic gas (He, Ne, Ar)
(B) Diatomic rigid-rotor gas (O₂, N₂, H₂ at room temp)
(C) Linear triatomic or vibrational diatomic gas (CO₂ at high temp)
(D) Non-linear polyatomic gas (CH₄, NH₃, H₂O vapour, rigid)
Column II:
(1) f = 3, γ = 5/3 = 1.67
(2) f = 5 (3 trans + 2 rot), γ = 7/5 = 1.40
(3) f = 7, γ = 9/7 = 1.29
(4) f = 6 (3 trans + 3 rot), γ = 4/3 = 1.33
explanation: Using C_V = (f/2)R, C_P = (f/2 + 1)R, and γ = 1 + 2/f.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following molecular speeds of a gas of molar mass M at absolute temperature T with their formulas:
Column I:
(A) Root Mean Square speed (v_rms)
(B) Average (Mean) speed (v_avg)
(C) Most Probable speed (v_mp)
(D) Speed of sound in the gas (v_sound)
Column II:
(1) √(3 R T / M) ≈ 1.732 √(RT/M)
(2) √(8 R T / π M) ≈ 1.596 √(RT/M)
(3) √(2 R T / M) ≈ 1.414 √(RT/M)
(4) √(γ R T / M)
explanation: Notice that v_rms > v_avg > v_mp > v_sound (in ratio √3 : √(8/π) : √2 : √γ).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following kinetic theory quantities with their mathematical expressions:
Column I:
(A) Pressure P exerted by an ideal gas in terms of translational KE per unit volume (E)
(B) Mean kinetic energy of a single gas molecule at temperature T (3 translational DOF)
(C) Mean free path (λ) of gas molecules (number density n, diameter d)
(D) Universal Gas Constant (R) in terms of Boltzmann constant (k_B) and Avogadro number (N_A)
Column II:
(1) P = (2 / 3) E = (1 / 3) ρ v_rms²
(2) (3 / 2) k_B T
(3) λ = 1 / (√2 π n d²)
(4) R = N_A k_B (≈ 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
explanation: Standard NCERT Kinetic Theory formulas.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following classical gas laws with the thermodynamic variables they relate:
Column I:
(A) Boyle's Law (constant T and n)
(B) Charles' Law (constant P and n)
(C) Gay-Lussac's Law (constant V and n)
(D) Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures
Column II:
(1) P₁ V₁ = P₂ V₂ (P ∝ 1/V)
(2) V₁ / T₁ = V₂ / T₂ (V ∝ T)
(3) P₁ / T₁ = P₂ / T₂ (P ∝ T)
(4) P_total = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ + ... for non-reacting gas mixture
explanation: Empirical gas laws unified into PV = nRT.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following molar heat capacities of an ideal gas with their expressions in terms of f and γ:
Column I:
(A) Molar heat capacity at constant volume (C_V)
(B) Molar heat capacity at constant pressure (C_P)
(C) Mayer's relation (C_P - C_V)
(D) Ratio of specific heats (γ = C_P / C_V)
Column II:
(1) (f / 2) R = R / (γ - 1)
(2) (f / 2 + 1) R = γ R / (γ - 1)
(3) R
(4) 1 + 2 / f
explanation: From equipartition of energy U = (f/2)nRT => C_V = (f/2)R, C_P = C_V + R, γ = 1 + 2/f.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Speed of sound in air is independent of pressure.
Reason (R): As pressure increases, density also increases proportionally at constant temperature, keeping P/rho constant.
options: A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.
explanation: v = sqrt(gamma × P / rho); for an ideal gas, P/rho = RT/M.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): CP is always greater than CV for an ideal gas (CP - CV = R).
Reason (R): At constant pressure, heat supplied is used for increasing internal energy as well as doing expansion work.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
explanation: Mayer's relation CP - CV = R because heat at constant pressure includes work done in expansion.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Velocity of sound in air increases with increase in temperature.
Reason (R): Speed of sound in ideal gas is v = √(γ R T / M), directly proportional to square root of temperature √T.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Laplace formula v = √(γ R T / M) shows speed of sound increases with √T.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The pressure of a gas is proportional to the mean kinetic energy of translation of its molecules per unit volume.
Reason (R): From kinetic theory, P = ⅓ ρ v_rms² = ⅔ (½ ρ v_rms²) = ⅔ E, where E is kinetic energy per unit volume.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: P = 2/3 E, which directly ties macroscopic pressure to microscopic kinetic energy density.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Light gases like hydrogen and helium escape from Earth's atmosphere, whereas nitrogen and oxygen do not.
Reason (R): The rms speed of hydrogen and helium at room temperature is comparable to or exceeds the escape velocity from Earth (11.2 km/s).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Since v_rms = √(3RT/M), smaller molar mass M results in much higher speeds, allowing light molecules in the upper atmosphere to escape.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): At absolute zero temperature (0 K), the kinetic energy of ideal gas molecules becomes zero.
Reason (R): According to kinetic theory of gases, translational kinetic energy of a molecule is given by E = 3/2 k_B T, which vanishes when T = 0 K.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Temperature is directly proportional to average molecular kinetic energy. Classically, at T = 0 K molecular motion ceases.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The mean free path of gas molecules decreases when pressure of the gas is increased at constant temperature.
Reason (R): Increasing pressure increases the number density n = P / (k_B T), which increases collision probability and shortens λ = 1 / (√2 π n d²).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Mean free path λ is inversely proportional to number density n. As pressure rises, molecules are packed closer, colliding more frequently.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Equal volumes of different ideal gases at the same temperature and pressure contain the same number of molecules.
Reason (R): In the ideal gas equation P V = N k_B T, if P, V, and T are identical, the total number of molecules N must be identical.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: This is Avogadro's hypothesis, which naturally follows from the ideal gas equation of state.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): At a given temperature T, the average translational kinetic energy of a Hydrogen (H₂) molecule is exactly equal to that of a heavy Oxygen (O₂) or Helium (He) molecule.
Reason (R): Average translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2) k_B T, which depends solely on absolute temperature T and is independent of molecular mass or atomicity.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Translational KE has 3 degrees of freedom for all gas molecules, so KE_trans = (3/2)k_B T depends only on T.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The root mean square (rms) speed of gas molecules at a constant temperature does not change when the pressure of the gas is doubled.
Reason (R): At constant temperature, as pressure P increases, the density ρ of the ideal gas increases in the exact same proportion, keeping P / ρ = R T / M constant.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: v_rms = √(3P/ρ) = √(3RT/M). At constant T, P/ρ stays constant, so v_rms is independent of pressure.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): According to the kinetic theory of gases, the collisions between ideal gas molecules and the walls of the container are perfectly elastic.
Reason (R): If molecular collisions were inelastic, the gas molecules would continuously lose kinetic energy and eventually settle down at the bottom, causing pressure and temperature to drop.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Elastic collisions ensure that the average kinetic energy and pressure of a thermally isolated gas remain constant over time.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): A real gas behaves most closely like an ideal gas at low pressure and high temperature.
Reason (R): At low pressure and high temperature, the volume occupied by the molecules themselves is negligible compared to the container volume, and intermolecular attractive forces are negligible compared to thermal kinetic energy.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Ideal gas assumptions (zero molecular volume b=0 and zero intermolecular attraction a=0) hold best when density is low and T is high.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: The law of equipartition of energy states that in thermal equilibrium, the average energy per molecule associated with each degree of freedom is ½ k_B T.
Statement II: For a monoatomic gas with 3 degrees of freedom, the total internal energy of one mole of gas is 3/2 R T.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Energy per degree of freedom = 1/2 k_B T. For 1 mole (N_A molecules) with 3 dof, U = 3 × 1/2 N_A k_B T = 3/2 RT.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: Real gases behave like ideal gases at high temperatures and low pressures.
Statement II: Under high temperature and low pressure, intermolecular forces are negligible and the volume occupied by gas molecules is negligible compared to container volume.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: At low P and high T, the van der Waals parameters a/V² and b become negligible, matching ideal gas conditions.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: The root mean square speed of oxygen molecules is greater than that of hydrogen molecules at the same temperature.
Statement II: The root mean square speed of gas molecules is inversely proportional to the square root of their molar mass: v_rms = √(3 R T / M).
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
explanation: Since M(O₂) = 32 and M(H₂) = 2, hydrogen has 4 times higher rms speed than oxygen at the same temperature.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: The total translational kinetic energy of any ideal gas depends only on its temperature and the number of moles, regardless of whether it is monoatomic or diatomic.
Statement II: The molar heat capacity at constant volume C_v is the same for all ideal gases.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Translational KE is always 3/2 nRT for any gas. But C_v depends on total degrees of freedom (3/2 R for monoatomic, 5/2 R for diatomic).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: The ratio of specific heats γ = C_p / C_v of a gas is always greater than 1.
Statement II: Adding heat at constant pressure requires additional energy to perform expansion work against atmospheric pressure.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: C_p = C_v + R > C_v, hence γ = C_p/C_v > 1. At constant P, heat goes into both internal energy and boundary work.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: For any gas in thermal equilibrium at temperature T, the molecular speeds follow the ordering: v_rms > v_avg > v_mp.
Statement II: The ratio v_mp : v_avg : v_rms is √2 : √(8/π) : √3 (or approximately 1 : 1.128 : 1.224).
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both statements are correct properties of the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: According to the law of equipartition of energy, each translational or rotational degree of freedom contributes ½ k_B T to the average energy per molecule, while each vibrational mode contributes k_B T.
Statement II: A vibrational mode has both kinetic energy (½ m v²) and potential energy (½ k x²), contributing 2 × (½ k_B T) = k_B T per molecule.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Each quadratic term in the Hamiltonian contributes ½ k_B T; a 1D harmonic oscillator has two quadratic terms (KE + PE), giving k_B T.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: For 1 mole of a solid crystalline element at high temperature (Dulong-Petit limit), the molar specific heat capacity is 3R.
Statement II: Each atom in a 3D crystalline solid vibrates along three mutually perpendicular axes (x, y, z), possessing 3 vibrational modes (6 quadratic energy terms).
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: U = 3 N_A k_B T = 3RT => C_V = dU/dT = 3R (Dulong-Petit law). Both statements are correct.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: When two non-reacting ideal gases with degrees of freedom f₁ and f₂ (moles n₁ and n₂) are mixed, the equivalent C_V of the mixture is (n₁ C_V1 + n₂ C_V2) / (n₁ + n₂).
Statement II: The effective adiabatic ratio γ_mix of the gas mixture is always the simple arithmetic average (γ₁ + γ₂) / 2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is true (from U_mix = U₁ + U₂). Statement II is false because γ_mix = C_P(mix) / C_V(mix) = (n₁C_P1 + n₂C_P2) / (n₁C_V1 + n₂C_V2), not (γ₁+γ₂)/2.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: If a vessel containing an ideal gas moves with a high uniform linear velocity v₀, the temperature of the gas inside the vessel increases.
Statement II: Temperature of a gas is a measure of the random (disordered) thermal kinetic energy of molecules in the center-of-mass frame, not the ordered bulk motion of the container.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is false and Statement II is true: ordered motion of the container does not alter random thermal motion or temperature.

subject: Physics
questionText: Degrees of freedom (f) for a Monoatomic gas (He, Ne, Ar), Diatomic rigid gas (N2, O2), and Non-linear Polyatomic gas (H2O, CH4) are respectively:

explanation: Mean free path λ = 1 / (√2 π n d²). λ increases with temperature and decreases with pressure.

subject: Physics
questionText: Collision frequency (Z) of gas molecules is related to mean free path λ and average velocity v_avg by:

questionText: At extremely high temperatures, when vibrational modes of diatomic molecules (like Cl2) are fully active, the molar heat capacity Cv becomes:

questionText: 50 mL of gas A effuses through an orifice in 100 seconds, while 50 mL of gas B effuses in 50 seconds. The ratio of molar masses MA / MB is:

questionText: For a gas molecule of mass m striking a container wall normally with speed u and rebounding elastically with speed u, the magnitude of momentum transferred to the wall in a single collision is:
explanation: Initial momentum = +mu, final momentum = -mu, so momentum imparted to the wall is Δp_wall = 2mu.

questionText: The mean free path λ of gas molecules at constant temperature T varies with gas pressure P as:
explanation: Since P = n k_B T => n = P / (k_B T), substituting into λ = 1 / (√2 π n d²) gives λ = k_B T / (√2 π d² P) ∝ 1/P at constant T.

subject: Physics
questionText: Which of the following gases has the maximum value of rms speed at a given room temperature (300 K)?
explanation: Since v_rms = √(3RT/M), the gas with the smallest molar mass M (H₂, M = 2 g/mol) has the highest rms speed.

subject: Physics
questionText: For one gram-mole of any ideal gas, the value of the product P V / T is always equal to:

subject: Physics
questionText: In a mixture of Helium (monoatomic, M = 4) and Oxygen (diatomic, M = 32) in thermal equilibrium at temperature T, the ratio of their total average kinetic energies per molecule (E_He / E_O2) is:

subject: Physics
questionText: The graph between (P V) on the y-axis and Pressure (P) on the x-axis for a given mass of an ideal gas at constant temperature T is:

A straight line passing through the origin
explanation: By Boyle's law, at constant T, PV = nRT = constant, so PV vs P is a horizontal line parallel to the P-axis.

subject: Physics
questionText: An ideal gas undergoes a reversible adiabatic expansion where its volume doubles (V2 = 2 V1). If the ratio of specific heats gamma = 1.5, what will be the final temperature T2 in terms of initial temperature T1?
explanation: For a reversible adiabatic process, T × V^(gamma - 1) = constant. Thus T2 = T1 × (V1 / V2)^(gamma - 1) = T1 × (1/2)^(1.5 - 1) = T1 × (1/2)^(0.5) = T1 / sqrt(2).

subject: Physics
questionText: Two moles (n1 = 2) of a monoatomic gas (He, Cv1 = 3R/2) at temperature T0 and three moles (n2 = 3) of a rigid diatomic gas (O2, Cv2 = 5R/2) at temperature 2T0 are mixed together in a thermally insulated (adiabatic) rigid container of fixed total volume. Find the final equilibrium temperature (T_mix) and the effective adiabatic exponent (gamma_mix) of the gas mixture:
explanation: 1) In an adiabatic rigid vessel (Q = 0, W = 0), total internal energy is conserved (Delta U = 0): n1 Cv1 (T_mix - T0) + n2 Cv2 (T_mix - 2T0) = 0 => 2(3R/2)(T_mix - T0) + 3(5R/2)(T_mix - 2T0) = 0 => 6(T_mix - T0) + 15(T_mix - 2T0) = 0 => 21 T_mix = 36 T0 => T_mix = (12 / 7) T0! And 2) Cv_mix = (n1 Cv1 + n2 Cv2)/(n1 + n2) = (3R + 7.5R)/5 = (21/10)R, Cp_mix = Cv_mix + R = (31/10)R => gamma_mix = Cp_mix / Cv_mix = 31 / 21!

subject: Physics
questionText:

(B) Velocity as a function of position
(C) Acceleration as a function of position
(D) Maximum acceleration
Column II:
(1) x = A sin(ωt + φ)
(2) v = ± ω √(A² - x²)
(3) a = -ω² x
(4) a_max = ω² A (at extremes x = ±A)
explanation: Fundamental equations of kinematic variables in simple harmonic motion.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the oscillating systems in Column I with their time period formulas in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Simple Pendulum of length l
(B) Spring-block system of mass m and spring constant k
(C) Two identical springs in parallel (mass m)
(D) Two identical springs in series (mass m)
Column II:
(1) 2π √(l / g)
(2) 2π √(m / k)
(3) 2π √(m / 2k)
(4) 2π √(2m / k)
explanation: Parallel springs: k_eff = 2k => T = 2π√(m/2k). Series springs: k_eff = k/2 => T = 2π√(2m/k).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the organ pipe harmonic frequencies in Column I with Column II (pipe length L, speed of sound v):
Column I:
(A) Fundamental frequency of Open organ pipe
(B) Fundamental frequency of Closed organ pipe
(C) Harmonics present in Open pipe
(D) Harmonics present in Closed pipe
Column II:
(1) v / (2L)
(2) v / (4L)
(3) All harmonics (1 : 2 : 3 : 4...)
(4) Only odd harmonics (1 : 3 : 5 : 7...)
explanation: Open pipe has nodes at both ends: f₁ = v/2L with all harmonics. Closed pipe has antinode at open and node at closed: f₁ = v/4L with odd harmonics only.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the wave phenomena in Column I with their physical criteria in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Beats
(B) Standing Waves (Stationary waves)
(C) Doppler Effect
(D) Resonance
Column II:
(1) Superposition of two sound waves of slightly different frequencies
(2) Superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions
(3) Apparent shift in frequency due to relative motion between source and observer
(4) Amplitude maximum when driving frequency equals natural frequency
explanation: Standard definitions of beats (Δf = f₁ - f₂), standing waves (nodes and antinodes), Doppler effect, and resonance.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the energy distributions in SHM in Column I with their values at displacement x = A/√2 in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Kinetic Energy (K)
(B) Potential Energy (U)
(C) Total Mechanical Energy (E)
(D) Ratio K / U
Column II:
(1) ½ E
(2) ½ E
(3) ½ k A²
(4) 1
explanation: U = 1/2 k x² = 1/2 k (A²/2) = 1/2 E. K = E - U = 1/2 E. Thus K = U and K/U = 1.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following oscillating systems with their time period formulas:
Column I:
(A) Simple pendulum of length L in uniform gravity g
(B) Mass m attached to two springs k₁ and k₂ in parallel
(C) Mass m attached to two springs k₁ and k₂ in series
(D) Liquid column of total length L in a vertical U-tube
Column II:
(1) T = 2π √(L / g)
(2) T = 2π √[m / (k₁ + k₂)]
(3) T = 2π √[m (k₁ + k₂) / (k₁ k₂)]
(4) T = 2π √(L / 2g)
explanation: Parallel springs: k_eq = k₁ + k₂; Series springs: k_eq = k₁k₂/(k₁+k₂); U-tube liquid column of total length L has restoring force 2Aρgx so T = 2π√(L/2g).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following standing wave resonators with their harmonic frequency ratios and fundamental wavelengths:
Column I:
(A) Stretched string fixed at both ends (length L)
(B) Open organ pipe (open at both ends, length L)
(C) Closed organ pipe (closed at one end, length L)
(D) Beat frequency produced by two tuning forks of frequencies f₁ and f₂
Column II:
(1) f₁ = v / (2L), harmonics 1 : 2 : 3 : 4...
(2) f₁ = v / (2L), all harmonics 1 : 2 : 3 : 4...
(3) f₁ = v / (4L), only odd harmonics 1 : 3 : 5...
(4) f_beat = |f₁ - f₂|
explanation: Both stretched string and open pipe support all harmonics (λ₁ = 2L); closed pipe supports only odd harmonics (λ₁ = 4L).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following instantaneous quantities in Simple Harmonic Motion (x = A sin ωt) with their values at mean (x = 0) and extreme (x = ±A) positions:
Column I:
(A) Velocity v = ω √(A² - x²)
(B) Acceleration a = -ω² x
(C) Kinetic Energy K = ½ m ω² (A² - x²)
(D) Potential Energy U = ½ m ω² x² (taking U(0) = 0)
Column II:
(1) Maximum (ωA) at mean position, zero at extreme
(2) Zero at mean position, maximum (ω²A) at extreme
(3) Maximum (½mω²A²) at mean, zero at extreme
